name: Beth-rapha
overview: Beth-rapha is a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Eshton. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, without additional narrative details or notes. His lineage situates him within the broader context of Judah's family lines.
namesAndTitles: The name Beth-rapha means "house of Rapha," which is understood as "house of healing." This proper name, found in 1 Chronicles 4:12, reflects a Hebrew origin and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Beth-rapha is the son of Eshton, as noted in 1 Chronicles 4:12. Beyond this paternal relationship, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Beth-rapha's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical record of Judah, emphasizing the faithfulness of God in preserving the lineage through which the Messiah would eventually come. Although the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal story, his mention affirms the detailed preservation of Israel's family heritage as recorded in Scripture.
